correctness.rationale: On a loopless even clique, nonbalanced nonunanimous states reach the majority consensus in one update, and balanced configurations complement with no fixed point: closed two-cycles pair distinct complements. On odd order 2r+1, a one-vote layer has r+1 independent tied agents while the initially minority agents are forced to the other color. For each critical row, a=2^(-r-1) is the swap probability and also the direct consensus probability for the current majority; b=(r+1)a is the stay probability. Since a+b<1, these layers are transient and all other nonunanimous states stabilize the next round. Color symmetry gives minority win a/(1-b+a), and the first-step time is 1+(a+b)E+1-2a-b. Its solution 2+b/(1-a-b) strictly decreases from 4 at r=1 to 2; the reversal probability is asymptotic to 2^(-r-1). Conditioning on the binomial count, including the endpoint masses and the even-layer zero entry time, gives both Bernoulli-start formulas for all p.
residual_risks: The replay tests lumped classes only. Actual even balanced recurrent classes are complement pairs, as proved by the configuration update, not singleton balanced-count states in configuration space.
The proof uses simultaneous updates, no self-loops, and conditionally independent fair tie choices.

value.rationale: The natural dense benchmark has a nontrivial parity distinction: balanced even cliques enter deterministic blinking immediately, whereas odd cliques stabilize to consensus and can reverse a strict majority only at the one-vote margin. The exact exponentially decreasing reversal probability and sharp bounded mean are quantitative benchmarks on an unbounded family, rather than a routine rediscovery of the triangle or an empirical small-size fit.
residual_risks: This gives neither constant-time stabilization for general graphs nor a bound on each realized odd-clique stabilization time.
